assertions.interpretation: The scene opens with Jia Chong initially drafting the legal statutes, marking the beginning of the law-making process.
Jia Chong and Yang Hu together consulted Grand Tutor Zheng Chong during the drafting process, a contemporaneous event within the scene.
Background: Jia Chong began his career as a Shangshu and was promoted to Tingwei (Commandant of Justice), prior to the law-drafting scene.

assertions.exact_span: 善刑法由此與散騎常侍裴楷共定科令
assertions.interpretation: Background: Because of his expertise in penal law, Jia Chong subsequently worked with Pei Kai to fix the statutes, contextualizing his role in the law-drafting.
assertions.surface: 善刑法由此與散騎常侍裴楷共定科令

assertions.interpretation: Later outcome: After the Jin dynasty received the abdication (of Wei), Jia Chong was enfeoffed as Duke of Lu Commandery.
Later outcome: Jia Chong died and was posthumously granted the title of Grand Chancellor (Taizai).
Later outcome: The statutes drafted were adopted as the Jin legal code.

assertions.exact_span: 累遷司徒太保晉受禪進太傅
assertions.interpretation: Background for Zheng Chong: He was successively promoted to Situ and Taibao, and after Jin received the abdication, advanced to Grand Tutor — the title he holds in the scene.
assertions.surface: 累遷司徒太保晉受禪進太傅

assertions.exact_span: 羊曰上意欲令小加弘潤

assertion.exact_span: 初文帝命荀勗賈充裴秀等分定禮儀律令
assertion.interpretation: Background: Earlier, Emperor Wen (Sima Zhao) ordered Xun Xu, Jia Chong, Pei Xiu and others to separately fix ritual and legal statutes, providing the origin of the law-drafting project.

assertion.interpretation: Background: All such statutes were first consulted with Zheng Chong before being implemented, explaining why Jia Chong and Yang Hu consulted him in the scene.
